doc.title: Carmen Lundy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 15, 2023

title: Voice teachers Mary Henderson Buckley and Robert Brewster
summary: Her classical teachers tolerated her jazz leanings; Buckley brought Roitstein into lessons and Brewster became her teacher.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Did the classical music voice teachers ever say to you, “I don’t like what I’m hearing, where is this coming from? Are you doing jazz? Or were you blessed with open-minded profs?

Yes. Yes, yes, yes, yes, yes. Mary Henderson Buckley was my first voice teacher at the University of Miami and Mary Henderson Buckley flat out, straight up, classical voice. Okay? And I studied with her for my first two and a half years, or something like that. We’re talking a while ago. And something interesting occurred. And the cool thing about Mary Henderson Buckley was she knew that I was kind of floating back and forth and there’s something called a jury where every Friday at noon classical vocalists, you know, the jazz artists, you had to perform for the faculty. That was the way it was. And these juries were where I kind of got, you know they were allowing me to kind of present the other side of what I was exploring so I would do the aria and then I would do some other kind of pop tune or whatever. But the cool thing was she knew David was upstairs in the jazz department and she’d bring him in for some of my lessons to hear me work with the tune or whatever I was going to do, the non-classical tune. So it just so happened that her experience introduced her to musical theater. So she was very familiar with all of those tunes that jazz artists took from the theater and turned into jazz standards. Sorry that’s my ride cymbal. So Mary Henderson Buckley was a super cool person and she was a great teacher, and all we did was seriously work on my technique and there was a portion of my lesson, a 90-minute lesson, wherein maybe the last twenty, thirty minutes was where we’d kind of work on a song, or work on whatever it was, the aria, the jazz standard, whatever. So Mary Henderson Buckley, I think she was very instrumental in talking them into allowing me to switch majors and go into the studio music and jazz major. And then, two and a half years later a gentleman moved from Germany to Miami to become the head of the voice department at the University of Miami. And his name was Dr. Robert Brewster. Dr. Robert Brewster was a black man who was the tenor. You know he was the tenor. And he got this job and apparently he moved back to the United States because his mother had become ill and he wanted to return to the United States and he became the head of the classical department, the voice classical department. And he was my teacher. So he became my teacher. And he was also very, he was an incredible pianist by the way. An incredible pianist as well as an amazing vocalist. So this was a continuation of this. And I was just allowed to pursue every avenue without any real pushback from anyone. I never really — I can’t remember ever being told oh no, no you must not, and you can not. That never happened.
